faq_logTimeReminders_q: Can WitnessWork remind me to log time for a day I planned?
faq_logTimeReminders_a: Yes. Go to Preferences → Plans, turn on Remind Me to Log Time, and choose a Remind At time (8:00 PM unless you change it). If a day has a plan but no time logged, you get one reminder at that time after the day's plans end: a morning plan reminds you that evening, and a plan still going at your Remind At time reminds you the next day. Several plans on the same day give one reminder, and when two days' reminders would arrive at the same time they're combined. Logging any time for that day stops its reminder and clears one you've already received; removing that day's plans or turning the setting off does too. A day planned with no time doesn't remind you, and days you missed before turning the setting on aren't included. Tapping the reminder opens Add Time with the date, planned time, and type already filled in. The reminder is also listed in the Home bell for a week, even if system notifications are off. The setting appears when you track hours; Regular Publishers turn on Log my hours first. Turning it on asks for notification permission, or opens your device settings if you've declined before. Reminders are worked out on your device from your own plans and time and aren't sent anywhere. Each device schedules its own reminders up to two weeks ahead, so open WitnessWork at least every two weeks to keep them coming. If you log time on another device, open WitnessWork on this one so it can cancel that day's reminder. On Android, the system may deliver a reminder a few minutes late to save battery. If reminders don't arrive, check that notifications are allowed for WitnessWork in your device settings and that Focus or Do Not Disturb isn't silencing them. If they still don't arrive, report the problem from the Help Center without including names or other private details.
faq_streaks_a: Your streak counts how consistently you keep the plans you make. For pioneers and other roles that log hours, each planned day you log any time on adds one, even if you log less than you planned. Days without a plan don't add to it or end it, so plan the days you mean to go out. For publishers, each month you share in the ministry adds one, whether you mark the month on Home or log time. Your streak shows on Home's header and your Profile once it reaches 3. When it's about to end, tap it on Home to log the day that's due. To see how Schedule and streaks work again, tap the question mark in Schedule's header.
faq_streakEnds_q: When does my streak end, and how do I keep it?
faq_streakEnds_a: A planned day can still be logged until the end of the next day. If that passes with no time logged for it, your streak ends. When yours is about to end, the flame on Home shows the time left, and a Streak Reminder comes at 6:00 PM on the last day. For publishers, a month can be recorded until the end of the next month, and the reminder comes three days before that month is over. If you can't go out on a planned day, remove that day's plan ahead of time: tap it on Schedule, tap More (•••), then Delete → Delete This Plan. For a recurring plan, only that date is removed. If you went out but forgot to log it, add the time on that day and your streak comes back. Turn Streak Reminders off in Preferences → Plans. They need notifications allowed for WitnessWork.
faq_streakBuddies_q: Can my buddies see my streak?
faq_streakBuddies_a: Yes, once it reaches 3, if you share it. Your buddies see the number on your card in their Buddies list, not your time or reports. It's end-to-end encrypted like the rest of what you share. To stop sharing it, open Buddies Settings and turn off Streak. A streak that ended stops showing on your buddies' phones even if your app hasn't opened since.
faq_navigationShortcuts_q: How do I navigate with keyboard shortcuts on iPad?
faq_navigationShortcuts_a: Connect a hardware keyboard to an iPad running iPadOS 26 or later, then hold Command while the main navigation is visible. Small shortcut labels appear beside the bottom tabs or sidebar items. Press Command and the displayed number to open that screen; release Command to hide the labels. Numbers follow the visible navigation order, so by default Home is Command 1 and Contacts is Command 2. Other numbers depend on which items are visible, including Settings in the sidebar. Close any open form or other screen before using these navigation shortcuts; they do not save or discard records. Only shortcut use is measured, not what you type. Support requires an installed app build with the keyboard feature and is unavailable on iPhone and Android. If labels do not appear, check that the keyboard is connected, return to the main navigation, and update and reopen the app. You can always tap navigation items instead. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep contact details out of public reports.

faq_pointerHover_q: How do I use a trackpad, mouse, or Apple Pencil on iPad?
faq_pointerHover_a: Connect a trackpad or mouse to your iPad, or hover a supported Apple Pencil just above the screen. Buttons, rows, and calendar days highlight as the pointer moves over them. When the sidebar is narrowed to icons, resting the pointer on an icon shows its name; other icon-only buttons, such as the map controls and Notifications, also show their names. Hover over the activity grid, the Service Year pace chart, or a mileage bar to see its date and value. On the map, hover a pin to see the contact's name, or hover a contact in the map's side list to name its pin. A secondary click (two-finger click) opens the same menu and preview as touching and holding. The sidebar's resize bar shows arrows for the directions it can still move, and two-finger scrolling moves a contact photo while you crop it. Everything is still available by touch: tap, touch and hold, or drag as usual. Hover changes nothing in your records. Only the fact that a pointer or Pencil was used is measured, at most once a day; no positions, names, or values are sent. On Android, a mouse highlights rows and shows names and chart values, but pins on the map don't show names on hover. iPhone has no hover. If nothing responds, check that the trackpad, mouse, or Pencil is connected, then update and reopen the app. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep contact details out of public reports.
faq_menuBar_q: How do I use the menu bar on iPad?
faq_menuBar_a: On iPadOS 26 or later, use Windowed Apps or Stage Manager and swipe down from the top edge to reveal the menu bar. After setup, WitnessWork Preferences opens in-app settings; the standard Settings item opens your device's settings. File opens Add Time when hours logging is enabled, Add Contact, New Plan, and Backup & Restore. Edit → Find Contact opens the Contacts list and focuses search. Help opens the Help Center, What's New, your email app for private support, or Check for Update. These shortcuts reuse the existing screens; opening a form does not save or share your records. Check for Update checks for a compatible app update and uses the existing download and restart flow when one is available. It cannot install a new native app version, and is unavailable in development builds. Menu-bar support requires an installed app build that includes it and is unavailable on iPhone and Android. If items are missing, update from your app store and reopen WitnessWork. You can still use the same actions inside the app. For other problems, use the Help Center's private email link and keep contact details and backups out of public reports.

1300.c7: Contact pin colors on Contact Details Screen now matches the map screen.
1300.c9: Month and annual total calculations now properly limit your credit time to 55 hours per month. Standard time is not affected by this rule. If you exceed this time using credit, you'll have overage displayed on your month's details screen.
1300.c10: Added time credit support. Existing users will be able to update their old time entries automatically.
1300.c11: Resolved issue with add button overlapping compass on iOS.

1310.c1: Greatly improved performance when navigating to time related screens.
1310.c3: Resolve date localization issue that occurred in some regions.
1310.c4: Updated styles and locations of commonly used items. Month and Service Year reports can be easily accessed in the tab bar at the bottom of the screen.
1310.c5: Resolved style overflow issues that occurred on certain screen sizes for the map screen.
1310.c6: Now automatically prefills recently used addresses when creating multiple contacts on the same day.
1310.c7: You can now toggle visibility of the home screen sections. Visit Preferences > Home Screen.
1310.c8: The app now is named WitnessWork, formerly 'JW Time' due to legal reasons.
1310.c9: Languages now attempt to find your exact region, otherwise it falls back to any locale with your language. If nothing can be found, it defaults to English.
1310.c10: Bemba language added! We need your help to translate. Please visit Settings > Help Translate

1320.c1: Now create coordinate only contacts. If your territory is very rural or with bad mapping information, there is now no need to rely on an address.
1320.c2: Easily toggle between device, dark, and light mode color scheme. Visit Preferences > Appearance.
1320.c4: 'Add Time' screen now allows for increments of 1 minute.
1320.c5: Added Kinyarwanda language, fully translated by Semana D. Thank you so much for your help!
1320.c6: You can now select how your time is displayed. Choose between decimal like: 13.5 or choose 13 Hrs 30 Mins. Visit Preferences > Appearance.

1330.c1: Added language selector. See Preferences to manually adjust your language.
1330.c2: Resolved issue with one-time plan having an inaccurate maximum date.

1340.c1: Added a special reward for when you check off your time box or add time!
1340.c2: You can now set a decimal value for hour goals on 'custom' publisher type.

1350.c1: You can now use autocomplete to search for an address! Just start typing to see suggestions. This feature is only possible by your generous donations. Thank you for your support!
1350.c2: Resolved issue where day sheet would not close automatically when adding time to a day of month.
1350.c3: Resolved overflow issue on home screen for tablets.

1360.c1: New: Share Contacts and easily import them. Transferring calls is now easier than ever.
1360.c2: You can now customize the colors of the pins on the map.
1360.c3: New: Dismiss Contact feature. You can now dismiss contacts you no longer wish to visit and receive notifications when it's time to return to them.
1360.c4: Added notes support to time reports.
1360.c5: Enhanced recurring plan scheduling - You can now schedule plans monthly by day of week (e.g., 'first Monday of every month').
1360.c7: Added statistics sections to your Monthly and Yearly reports to better track your progress and patterns.
1360.c8: You can now change your calendar's first day of the week. Visit Preferences > Appearance.
1360.c10: Follow up topic now supports multiple lines.
1360.c11: There are now no restrictions on when you can add time or schedule plans.
1360.c12: Added visual indicators on calendar days to show when notes are present.
1360.c13: Resolves issue with Korean and Panama phone number formatting.
1360.c14: Contact Details Screen map is now zoomed out to easily see surroundings at a glance.
1360.c15: Fixed various navigation issues when adding time and scheduling plans.
1360.c16: Improved readability and consistency throughout the app with better spacing and button sizes.

1382.c1: The Milestone Update is here. A whole new look with a floating tab bar, frosted cards, and a fresh, modern feel throughout the app.
1382.c2: New Contacts tab with fuzzy search, smart sort, and stacked filters. Your contacts are now a first-class destination.
1382.c3: Progress Screen 2.0: a fresh look at Month, Year, and All-time, with customizable milestones, category breakdowns, and lifetime hours.
1382.c4: iCloud sync arrives (Supporter): your reports, contacts, and plans stay in step across all your devices. Optional photo sync keeps avatars synced too.
1382.c5: Onboarding has been rebuilt from the ground up. A personal note from the developer, animated plan previews, and a checklist tailored to your goals.
1382.c6: Brand new home screen widgets: month calendar, appointments, hours, and contacts. All one tap away.
1382.c7: Contact avatars are here. Photos or emoji, with a tap-to-expand fullscreen viewer.
1382.c8: Share a contact with another publisher via secure universal links.
1382.c9: Smarter recurring plans. Schedule by day-of-week and week-of-month, with per-instance overrides and deletions.
1382.c10: Time rollover: fractional minutes carry forward into the next month, manually or automatically.
1382.c11: Beautiful new celebrations the moment you cross a goal.
1382.c12: New Supporter tier with personalization, including a custom accent color.
1382.c13: Schedule screen: a focused calendar view of day plans and recurring conversations.
1382.c14: A redesigned profile card on the home screen showing your role, time served, and fun stats.
1382.c15: Approaching and missed conversations now surface on the home screen so you never lose track.
1382.c16: Phone region code now persists across new contacts. Phone region search is faster and more accurate.
1382.c17: Map empty state, location prompts, and contact map clustering have all been polished.
1382.c18: Countless small bug fixes, performance improvements, and visual refinements throughout the app.

1383.c1: Plans now have a Type. Assign a category to a scheduled plan and your projected totals reflect the right kind of credit.
1383.c2: Projected totals are more accurate. They respect your monthly credit cap and no longer double-count time you've already logged today.
1383.c3: The celebration chime once again respects your ring/silent switch.
1383.c5: New contacts and address edits now save immediately, even before the geocode api finishes locating them.
1383.c6: The calendar refreshes right away after you add, edit, or remove a plan.
1383.c7: Map pins stay in focus after you tap them. Resolve intermittent issue with map refocusing incorrect contact pin.
1383.c8: Smoother scrolling in the Contacts list. Resolve issues with contacts disappearing.
1383.c4: Your Donations now shows the correct billing period and price for annual and granted supporter subscriptions.

1400.c1: Switching from MyTime? You can now import your contacts and visit history straight from a MyTime backup, with a preview before anything is added, so there's no manual re-entry.
1400.c2: Date format, clock style, and start of the week are now separate from your app language. Set each one in Settings > Date & Time, with an Auto option that follows your region or device.
1400.c3: You can now customize the day thresholds and colors behind contact staleness. Tune them in Settings > Personalization > Color Key.
1400.c4: Resolved an issue with the map search auto closing.
1400.c5: Locating contacts on the map now shows live progress, and you can skip it midway without losing your place.
1400.c6: Faster, smoother scrolling in the Contacts list, plus quicker home screen widget updates.
1400.c7: Fixed projected totals around time zone changes, enlarged header buttons for easier tapping, and polished countless small details throughout the app.

1411.c1: New: Meet Scribe AI. Paste your field-ministry notes, whether a handwritten-style log or an export from another app, and Scribe AI turns them into contacts, visits, and time entries for you to review before anything is saved. Refine the results by chatting inline, start an import right from onboarding, and never lose a credit on an import that finds nothing.
1411.c2: A new customizable This Month dashboard on the home screen. Your goal, projection, and schedule pace live in cards you can arrange and expand, while your Service Report stays in one clean card. Tap the report for a full breakdown.
1411.c3: Monthly goal overrides. Set a different goal for a single month when your circumstances change, and see your planned hours as their own progress ring.
1411.c4: Plan more than one thing per day. Day plans on the same date now add together, each keeping its own category, and plans that do not count toward a day are clearly marked.
1411.c5: Easier editing everywhere. Plans, time entries, and conversations now have an ellipsis menu for Edit and Delete, and recurring plans offer clear choices for changing one date, future dates, or the whole series.
1411.c6: Service Reports: Hourglass and NW Publisher submission are back, you can pick a default submission method, edit the report comment before sending, and get a month-end reminder. The year-by-year history can now be trimmed or backfilled with earlier years.
1411.c7: Schedule now shows each day's status at a glance: ahead, behind, on track, upcoming, matched, or no plan.
1411.c8: Supporter status now follows your Apple ID across devices, Scribe AI allowances roll over on a schedule, and the Supporter screen has been simplified.
1411.c9: Fixed time entries and plans landing on the wrong day in time zones at UTC+12 and beyond, plus wrong-day dates late in the evening west of UTC. Fixed map pins opening the wrong contact after swiping the card carousel. Time rollover now keeps Credit Time in its original month by default.
1411.c10: The Credit toggle on categories is now available to every hours-based role. Also fixed a rare crash when closing a picker, restored favorite stars and the current-month Bible study icon, updated to Expo SDK 57, and trimmed the app size.

1420.c1: New iPad layouts show contacts, maps, and schedules alongside their details.
1420.c2: Customize contact fields: reorder phone, email, and custom fields, hide phone or email, and permanently delete archived custom fields.
1420.c3: See your logged time by category across the Service Year, and adjust the monthly credit limit in supported Publisher preferences.
1420.c4: Hourglass submissions now separate preaching time from Credit Time.
1420.c5: The calendar Assistant is available again, with controls in Schedule preferences.

1430.c1: Data protection mode for publishers in the EU, the UK and Switzerland keeps householder records to what the law allows, including consent tracking and cleanup of contacts you haven't visited in a while.
1430.c2: Create a contact right from a pin you drop on the map.
1430.c3: Kingdom Publishers can choose to log their hours with a timer, an optional monthly goal and the Progress tab.
1430.c4: The Year tab now shows your service-year total for every role, even without an annual goal.
1430.c5: Follow-ups on visits are now optional, and you can turn off app sounds in Preferences.
1430.c6: Fixed dates shifting for publishers in far-east time zones.

notesImport_disclosureTitle: How Scribe AI reads your notes
notesImport_disclosureBody: Scribe AI sends your notes to a third-party language model hosted in a privacy-friendly region under a zero-data-retention agreement. It reads your text and keeps nothing afterward. WitnessWork stores no copy of your notes on our servers, and nothing is added to your records until you review and confirm.

notesImport_privacySummary: Scribe AI sends your notes through OpenRouter to trusted Western language-model providers with Zero Data Retention, so they aren't stored. Notes are held only while the import runs; your history stays on your device. WitnessWork never sells or shares your notes or uses them to train models. Voice logs and photos are turned into text on your device; audio and images are never uploaded.

faq_timeRollover_q: Does my time automatically roll over to the next month?
faq_timeRollover_a: Yes. Partial hours below your monthly goal can carry over to the next month. Open Preferences → Publisher and turn on the rollover option. The carried hours appear automatically when the new month begins, so you don't need to manually subtract or re-enter anything.
faq_bibleStudies_a: Studies are tracked per contact, not per day. To count a study, open a contact, log a conversation, and mark it as "Conducted Bible Study." That contact will count as 1 study for the current month, even if you have multiple sessions with them. To raise your study count, mark a study conversation with a different contact.
faq_iCloudSync_q: Can I sync my data between devices?
faq_iCloudSync_a: iCloud Sync is a Supporter feature on iOS. Open Settings → iCloud Sync on each supported device using the same iCloud account to sync your service records, contacts, visits, and preferences. Photos have a separate Include images in sync switch. If a device signs in to a different Apple Account, iCloud Sync turns off there before any records are read or sent, and they stay on the device; turn sync back on to choose how to combine it with that account’s iCloud data. That device also stops sharing Supporter status from your previous account; if it was bought with this device’s App Store account, use Restore Purchases. A device set up from another device’s backup syncs as its own device automatically. Calendar Sync is a separate, free feature that publishes your upcoming Follow-ups to a dedicated calendar; it does not sync your app records between devices. On Android, Supporters sync between Android phones and tablets with Google Drive Sync instead (see “How do I sync my data between Android devices?”). Syncing between an iPhone and an Android device isn’t supported; use Settings → Backup & Restore to move a saved backup between them.
faq_googleDriveSync_q: How do I sync my data between Android devices?
faq_googleDriveSync_a: Google Drive Sync is a Supporter feature on Android, in beta. On each Android phone or tablet, open Settings → Google Drive Sync and turn on Sync with Google Drive, then choose the same Google Account in Google's window and allow WitnessWork to keep its data in your Google Drive. It syncs your service records, plans, contacts, visits, categories, mileage, profile, and shared preferences; photos have a separate Include images in sync switch. Each device has its own switch, and settings like data protection mode, analytics consent, and onboarding stay on each device. While WitnessWork is open, changes from your other devices arrive within about a minute, and otherwise the next time you open it; tap Sync now to check right away. On a new Android device, choose From Google Drive on the “Pick up where you left off” setup screen to restore your data, which also brings your Supporter status over once that Google Account is connected. If a device connects a different Google Account, sync turns off there before anything is read or sent, and your records stay on the device. Sync between an iPhone and an Android device isn’t supported; use Settings → Backup & Restore to move a backup between them.
faq_googleDriveSyncPrivacy_q: What does Google Drive Sync store, and who can see it?
faq_googleDriveSyncPrivacy_a: Each Android device keeps one copy of your WitnessWork data, plus optional photos, in a hidden app folder in the Google Drive of the account you connected. Only WitnessWork can open that folder: it doesn't appear in the Drive app or website, other apps can't read it, and WitnessWork can't see anything else in your Drive. Your data goes straight between your device and Google and never passes through WitnessWork's servers. Google stores it under your Google Account like your other Drive files; it isn't end-to-end encrypted. WitnessWork keeps only a one-way code for the connected account on the device, not your email. The folder counts against your Google storage. To remove it, turn off sync on every device, then in Google Drive on the web open Settings → Manage apps → WitnessWork → Options → Delete hidden app data. Disconnecting Google Drive in Settings → Google Drive Sync stops access from that device and leaves the folder for your other devices. To remove WitnessWork's access for every device, remove it under Third-party apps & services in your Google Account. Your JSON backups from Settings → Backup & Restore are separate and stay wherever you save them.
faq_googleDriveSyncTroubleshooting_q: Google Drive Sync isn't working on my Android device. What can I check?
faq_googleDriveSyncTroubleshooting_a: Open Settings → Google Drive Sync and read the status. Check that every device is connected to the same Google Account and that Google Play services is installed and up to date. If the status says to reconnect, tap Reconnect Google Drive and allow access again; Google asks again if access was removed in your Google Account settings. If your Google storage is full, your changes stay on this device until there's room; free up space or get more storage, then tap Sync now. Sync needs an internet connection; changes made offline are sent when you're back online and WitnessWork is open. If a device uses a newer version of WitnessWork, update every device. Google Drive Sync requires Supporter access; if it lapses, sync pauses and resumes when access returns. Keep an exported backup and the device with your latest data before rebuilding Google Drive data. Contact private support from the Help Center if syncing still fails, and keep householder details out of public reports.
faq_calendarSetup_q: How do I show Follow-ups in my calendar?
faq_calendarSetup_a: Calendar Sync is free on iPhone, iPad, and Android. This answer covers iPhone and iPad, and How does Calendar Sync work on Android? covers Android. During first-time setup, or from the invitation in the notifications tray after updating, tap Add to Calendar to create a WitnessWork calendar (in iCloud when available). You can also set it up anytime in Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync: allow full calendar access, then create a WitnessWork calendar or choose a calendar used only for WitnessWork. Updates need iCloud sign-in and an internet connection, even for Google or Outlook calendars. To use Google or Outlook, create a calendar with that provider, add the account in iPhone Settings → Apps → Calendar → Calendar Accounts, and turn on its calendars. Your default calendar and calendars stored only on this device can't be selected. Once a calendar is selected, every upcoming Follow-up is added automatically, including ones you already saved, as a 30-minute event. Calendar Sync adds all of your upcoming Follow-ups or none; to stop adding them, turn it off in Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync. Past Follow-ups, service Plans, and recurring Plans aren't added. Each event gets the same alert as its Follow-up's Notify Me reminder, and no alert when Notify Me is off. Your calendar provider may add its own default alerts; for Google, remove them under that calendar's Event notifications in Google Calendar settings. Make changes in WitnessWork, because calendar edits, including alerts, may be replaced on the next update.
faq_calendarPrivacy_q: What does Calendar Sync share or store?
faq_calendarPrivacy_a: By default, published events contain a generic Follow-up title, the appointment time and duration, and a link that opens the Visit in WitnessWork. Include names and addresses is optional and applies across your devices; turning it on adds those details to published events. Visit notes and Follow-up topics are never exported. Your chosen calendar provider may sync events to other devices, shared calendars, and widgets, so check that calendar's sharing settings before including details. WitnessWork manages only events it marked as its own and does not import your personal calendar appointments. A private iCloud record stores device names and opaque identifiers, publishing ownership, the connected calendar's name and account label, shared options, and event identifiers. Appointment content stays in the chosen calendar account. Each device's calendar identifier and connection state stay local and are separate from app-data sync and backup files.
faq_calendarPrimary_q: Why does Calendar Sync use a primary device?
faq_calendarPrimary_a: Exactly one device publishes your Follow-ups to avoid competing updates. The first device to connect becomes primary. On iOS devices using the same iCloud account, open Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync to register each device, view the Primary device list, and choose a primary. Calendar Sync itself does not require Supporter. Follow-ups edited on another device reach the primary through existing app-data sync, which still requires Supporter and enabled iCloud Sync; open WitnessWork on the primary to publish them. After a transfer, the new primary needs access to the same calendar account and full calendar permission. If a transfer is pending, reopen WitnessWork on the previous primary so it can finish its interrupted operation. There is no automatic timeout takeover if that device is permanently unavailable; use private support under Still need help? in the Help Center. Removing a stale device from the list does not delete its app records or calendar events.
faq_calendarTroubleshooting_q: Calendar events are missing or updates are paused. What should I do?
faq_calendarTroubleshooting_a: If Calendar Sync stops updating, a Calendar updates paused notification appears in the notifications tray (the bell on Home): right away when something needs you, such as calendar access, or after a day for problems that often clear on their own, like no internet connection. Tap it for the fix, or choose Turn Off if you no longer want Follow-ups in your calendar. You can also open Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync and read the displayed error. Check your internet connection, iCloud sign-in, calendar account, and full calendar access for WitnessWork in iPhone Settings. Use Sync now on the primary device after your calendar account and app data finish syncing. A missing calendar must be reconnected or replaced; calendars renamed outside WitnessWork may need to be chosen again. When a previously published future event is missing, updates pause even if this device published it: calendar sync delays, deletion, and moving an event can look the same. Wait for the calendar account to finish syncing and confirm you chose the same dedicated calendar. Move any WitnessWork events you moved elsewhere back before retrying. Restore missing events is an explicit recovery option after those checks; it can create duplicates if copies are still downloading or remain elsewhere. A past Follow-up is not initially added. For pending device transfers, reopen the previous primary. If the problem continues, use the Help Center's private support option and include the app version, device and operating-system version, and the error shown. Keep contact details, calendar screenshots, notes, and backups out of public reports.
faq_calendarDisconnect_q: What happens when I turn off Calendar Sync or uninstall WitnessWork?
faq_calendarDisconnect_a: In Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync, choose Turn Off Calendar Sync, or choose Turn Off on a Calendar updates paused notification. On the primary device, the one that updates your calendar, you can keep the events already added or remove them. Remove Events removes the marked events from the selected calendar, including previously exported history; unrelated events and the calendar itself remain. Turning it off on the primary stops updates from every device. On any other device, Calendar Sync turns off on that device only and the events stay. Events you keep, or that are left after uninstalling, are no longer updated until you set Calendar Sync up again. Uninstalling WitnessWork does not remove calendar events. You can remove an unused dedicated calendar in your calendar app after checking that it contains nothing you want to keep. Turning off Calendar Sync does not delete your Contacts, Visits, or Follow-ups in WitnessWork.
faq_calendarAndroid_q: How does Calendar Sync work on Android?
faq_calendarAndroid_a: Calendar Sync is free on Android. During first-time setup, from the invitation in the notifications tray, or in Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync, tap Add to Calendar or Choose a calendar, then allow calendar access. Create a WitnessWork calendar on this device, or choose an existing calendar used only for WitnessWork, such as one you created in Google Calendar and set to sync to this phone. A calendar created on the device stays on this device; a Google calendar also shows on your other devices and on the web. Main calendars can't be selected. Every upcoming Follow-up is then added as a 30-minute event with the same alert as its Notify Me reminder; Calendar Sync adds all of your upcoming Follow-ups or none. Past Follow-ups and Plans aren't added. Updates run when you open WitnessWork and after you save changes, and Sync now updates right away. Each event's description holds a WitnessWork link that identifies its Follow-up, so an update changes the existing event instead of adding another, even when another Android device updates the same Google calendar. Don't edit that link. An event you delete in your calendar app comes back on the next update. Android has no primary device and doesn't use iCloud, and Include names and addresses applies to this device only. If updates stop, for example because calendar access was turned off, a Calendar updates paused notification appears in the notifications tray; tap it for the fix, or open Calendar Sync to read the error, then use Open Settings or Sync now. Turn Off Calendar Sync keeps or removes WitnessWork events; it never deletes the calendar or your other events. Uninstalling WitnessWork leaves its events, so remove them first if you don't want them. If the problem continues, use the private support option under Still need help? in the Help Center, and keep contact details and calendar screenshots out of public reports.
faq_widgets_q: Are there home or lock screen widgets?
faq_widgets_a: Yes, on iOS. Long-press your home or lock screen, tap the + button, search for WitnessWork, and pick the widget you want. The hours widget shows your monthly progress at a glance.
faq_appleWatch_q: Is there an Apple Watch app?
faq_appleWatch_a: Yes, for iPhone with an Apple Watch on watchOS 26 or later. It installs automatically if Automatic App Install is on; otherwise open the Watch app on your iPhone, find WitnessWork under Available Apps, and tap Install. Then open WitnessWork on your iPhone once so your watch gets your progress. On the watch you can add time for today with an optional Type, start and pause your iPhone's timer, and save the timer's time as an entry. If you don't log hours as a Kingdom Publisher, you can mark that you shared the good news this month. Two complications can go on a watch face or in your Smart Stack: Monthly Progress shows your hours toward this month's goal, with a mark where your plans put you by today; in a round spot you can choose a ring or a gauge, with your goal at its end or a clock below, and without a goal it shows your hours alone. Up Next shows your next follow-up or plan. You can also use Siri on your watch to add time, start, pause or stop your timer, and log a mileage trip, with the same phrases as on iPhone, such as "Add time in WitnessWork" or "Log a trip in WitnessWork". Your iPhone keeps your records. The watch receives your monthly progress, report status, timer, Types, car names and distance unit, and for Up Next the name, address and topic of your follow-ups and the title and place of your plans for the next two weeks. It never receives notes or other contact details, and it can't edit or delete entries. The watch app needs your iPhone, so it isn't available for an Apple Watch set up with Family Setup. With an Android phone, use the Wear OS app instead.
faq_appleWatchUpNext_q: What does Up Next on my Apple Watch show?
faq_appleWatchUpNext_a: Up Next shows whichever comes first: your next follow-up or your next plan. Plans appear only if you log hours. Add the Up Next complication to a watch face or your Smart Stack: touch and hold your watch face and tap Edit, or use the Watch app on your iPhone. It's also on the watch app's home screen. A follow-up or plan stays up for 15 minutes after it starts, so you can check the address or topic when you arrive, and then the next one takes its place. A plan without a start time shows for its whole day, after that day's timed items. Missed follow-ups don't appear; find them in WitnessWork on your iPhone. Names and topics are hidden while your wrist is down or your watch is locked, because others may see your watch face. Tap Up Next to open it, then tap Directions for directions in Maps on your watch, or Start Timer to start your iPhone's service timer for a plan; the timer needs your iPhone nearby. Up Next looks two weeks ahead and keeps moving along while your iPhone is away. Changes you make on your iPhone reach your watch the next time they connect. If it's out of date, open WitnessWork on your iPhone, then on your watch. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep householder details out of public reports.
faq_siri_q: Can I use Siri or Shortcuts with WitnessWork?
faq_siri_a: Yes, on iPhone and iPad with iOS 17 or later, and on the Apple Watch app. Open WitnessWork once after updating, then say "Add time in WitnessWork" (or "Log time"), "Start my timer in WitnessWork", "Pause my timer in WitnessWork", "Stop my timer in WitnessWork", "Log a trip in WitnessWork" or "Log a round trip in WitnessWork". Siri listens in your Siri language, which can differ from the language you chose in WitnessWork. Siri asks how long or how far. Distances use your Mileage distance unit; for a round trip, say the one-way distance and it's doubled. Stopping the timer adds its whole minutes as an entry for today and resets it; with less than a minute, nothing is added. Time and trips are added for today, as Standard time and with the car you used last. To pick a Type or car, add the action in the Shortcuts app, where you can also run it from the Action Button or a Home Screen shortcut. Adding time and the timer need you to log hours (Regular Publishers turn on Log my hours first). Logging trips needs Track Mileage on and at least one car. On iPhone and iPad the timer changes right away, and time and trips you add with Siri are saved the next time you open WitnessWork, then reach your other devices with iCloud Sync like any entry. On the watch they're sent to your iPhone like other watch entries. Siri can only use your Types, car names, distance unit and timer from WitnessWork, never contacts, notes or reports. Siri and Shortcuts aren't available on Android. If Siri doesn't recognize a phrase, open WitnessWork once, wait a minute, and check that Siri is allowed for WitnessWork in Settings. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep your records out of public reports.
faq_appleWatchSync_q: Why does my Apple Watch say Syncing with iPhone?
faq_appleWatchSync_a: Time and trips you add on your watch are sent to your iPhone right away when it's nearby, or the next time they connect, and saved once WitnessWork runs on your iPhone. Until then your watch shows Syncing with iPhone. Its total and complications include that time right away, except Credit Time, which is added once your iPhone saves it and applies your monthly credit limit. Each entry keeps the day you added it on the watch, is saved only once even if it's sent again, and isn't brought back if you already deleted it on your iPhone. Saved entries reach your other devices with iCloud Sync like any other entry. Starting, pausing, stopping and saving the timer need your iPhone nearby. If the watch says the timer changed on your iPhone, check the time and try again. If your watch stays out of date, keep your iPhone nearby and unlocked, open WitnessWork on your iPhone, then open it on your watch. After your iPhone restarts, unlock it once before syncing. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep your records out of public reports.
faq_wearOs_q: Is there a Wear OS app?
faq_wearOs_a: Yes, for an Android phone with a watch on Wear OS 3 or later. Install WitnessWork from the Play Store on your watch, or from WitnessWork's Play Store page on your phone, then open WitnessWork on your phone once so your watch gets your progress. On the watch you can add time for today with an optional Type, start and pause your phone's timer, and save the timer's time as an entry. If you don't log hours as a Kingdom Publisher, you can mark that you shared the good news this month. Add the Monthly Progress and Up Next complications to a watch face, and the Monthly Progress tile to start or pause your timer or add time with a swipe. While your timer runs, it shows on your watch face with Pause and Stop; Stop adds the timer's whole minutes as an entry for today. Allow notifications when your watch asks, so the running timer can show there. Your phone keeps your records. The watch receives your monthly progress, report status, timer, Types, car names and distance unit, and for Up Next the name, address and topic of your follow-ups and the title and place of your plans for the next two weeks. It never receives notes or other contact details, and it can't edit or delete entries. Because others may see your watch, Up Next shows "Follow Up" instead of a name on watch faces, and in the app while your wrist is down; open it to see who it is. Wear OS can't add time or log trips by voice, so use the tile or the app instead. The watch app needs your phone with WitnessWork installed.
faq_wearOsSync_q: Why does my Wear OS watch say Syncing with phone?
faq_wearOsSync_a: Time you add on your watch is sent to your phone right away when it's nearby, or the next time they connect, and saved the next time you open WitnessWork on your phone. Until then your watch shows Syncing with phone. Its total, tile and complications include that time right away, except Credit Time, which is added once your phone saves it and applies your monthly credit limit. Each entry keeps the day you added it on the watch, is saved only once even if it's sent again, and isn't brought back if you already deleted it on your phone. Starting, pausing, stopping and saving the timer need your phone nearby, even if WitnessWork isn't open on it. If the watch says the timer changed on your phone, check the time and try again. If your watch stays out of date, check that it's connected to your phone in your watch's companion app, keep your phone nearby, open WitnessWork on your phone, then open it on your watch. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep your records out of public reports.
faq_switchingPioneer_q: How do I switch between Publisher and Auxiliary Pioneer mid-month?
faq_switchingPioneer_a: Open Preferences → Publisher Status and choose what fits right now: Publisher, Auxiliary Pioneer, Regular Pioneer, Special Pioneer, Circuit Overseer, or Custom. Goals and totals adjust to match. Switch back when you're done. Past months keep the time you entered, so your history stays accurate.
faq_submitReport_q: Does the app submit my service report for me?
faq_submitReport_a: WitnessWork doesn't send your report anywhere by itself. How and to whom you submit is up to you and your service committee. Open a month's Field Service Report, choose a method from the dropdown above the Submit button, and tap Submit. You can copy a plain-text summary, share it, or hand it straight to Hourglass or NW Publisher, which opens with your hours, Credit, and Bible studies filled in for you to review and send. NW Publisher only accepts the previous month's report. WitnessWork remembers your choice; you can also change it in Preferences → Submission method.
faq_remainingHours_q: How do I see how many hours I have left this month or year?
faq_remainingHours_a: Open the Progress tab from the bottom bar. The Month sub-screen shows time so far and hours left for the current month. Pioneers can switch to the Year sub-screen to see annual goal progress, time so far, remaining hours, and a per-month breakdown comparing actual hours to plan.
faq_goalPacing_q: How can I tell if I'm ahead or behind on my hour goal?
faq_goalPacing_a: Open the Progress tab from the bottom bar. The Month sub-screen shows your daily target so you can see if you're on track for the current month. Pioneers can switch to the Year sub-screen, where the Service Year Pace chart shows how far ahead or behind your Annual Goal you are today, and each month's bar shows how that month did against its goal.
faq_serviceYearPace_q: How do I read the Service Year Pace chart?
faq_serviceYearPace_a: Open the Progress tab and switch to Year. If your status has an Annual Goal, such as regular pioneer, the Service Year Pace card appears below your milestones. The dashed gray line is where your Annual Goal puts you by the end of each month. It is built from each month's own goal, so a mid-year appointment or an auxiliary pioneer month changes it, but a Monthly Goal you changed yourself does not. The green line is your time so far, counted the same way as your Service Report, including each month's credit limit. The dashed green line adds the time you have planned. The faint line is last service year, shown when you logged time in it, and the number at its end is last year's total. If a line runs well past your Annual Goal, the space above the goal is drawn on a compressed (logarithmic) scale so the months below stay readable. Press and hold the chart, then slide your finger, to see any month's totals. "Ahead of pace" compares your time with where the goal line is today. Below the card, each month has a bar: solid for logged time, lighter for credit time, and striped for plans, with a tick at that month's goal. The key above the months explains these marks, and the Hours and vs Goal columns give the numbers. Every bar uses the same scale, so you can compare months. Without an Annual Goal you see the month bars but not the chart. If a month looks wrong, press and hold it to change its status or goal. The chart is drawn on your device from your own entries and isn't shared.
faq_timeFormat_q: Can I display time as "1h 30m" instead of "1.5"?
faq_timeFormat_a: Yes. Open Preferences → Appearance and choose your preferred time format. Both formats are available everywhere time is shown.
faq_weekStart_q: Can I start the week on Monday instead of Sunday?
faq_weekStart_a: Yes. Preferences → Appearance lets you choose the first day of the week. The change applies to the calendar, schedule, and any other weekly views.
faq_darkMode_q: Can I force dark mode or light mode?
faq_darkMode_a: Yes. Open Preferences → Appearance → Color Scheme and pick System, Light, or Dark. The app will stop following your phone's setting and use the one you choose.
faq_appIcon_q: Can I change the app's icon?
faq_appIcon_a: Alternate app icons are a Supporter perk on iOS. Open Settings → Personalization → App Icon and choose an alternate. Alternate app icons are unavailable on Android.
faq_reorderHome_q: Can I reorder the cards on my home screen?
faq_reorderHome_a: Yes. Open Preferences → Home Screen to show, hide, and reorder cards. The home screen will keep your custom layout going forward.
faq_reorderTabs_q: Can I change the order of the tabs?
faq_reorderTabs_a: Yes. Open Settings → Preferences → Tab Order and use the up and down arrows beside each tab, or long-press a tab's name to move it to the top or bottom. The new order applies right away to the bottom bar on phones and the sidebar on tablets, on iOS and Android. Tabs can be reordered but not hidden. WitnessWork still opens on Home, and Progress only appears for roles that log hours; it keeps its place in your order if you change roles. On iPad, Command-number keyboard shortcuts follow your order too. The order is a preference, so it's included in backups and syncs with iCloud when sync is on; it doesn't change any of your records. To go back, move the tabs back to Home, Contacts, Progress, Schedule. If the order doesn't update, restart the app and use Still need help? below.
faq_timerRounding_q: Why was my timer rounded to the nearest 5 minutes?
faq_timerRounding_a: That was old behavior. Recent versions save the exact stopwatch time when you stop the timer, with no rounding. If you're still seeing 5-minute rounding, update the app to the latest version.
faq_addNotesToTime_q: Can I add notes to a time entry?
faq_addNotesToTime_a: Yes. When you add or edit a time entry, you can attach a note (e.g. "cart witnessing" or "cut short"). You can also tag entries with categories so similar entries stay grouped in your time reports.
faq_specialPioneerAnnual_q: I'm a special pioneer, why is the app showing me an annual goal?
faq_specialPioneerAnnual_a: Special pioneers don't have an annual goal by default. If yours appears, open Preferences → Publisher and turn off the annual goal. Your monthly goal stays in place and the annual bar on the Progress tab's Year sub-screen will be hidden.
faq_ldcCreditCap_q: Are LDC and other credit hours included in my totals?
faq_ldcCreditCap_a: Yes. Credit hours count toward your monthly hour total. For the service-year total, up to 55 credit hours per month are counted, in line with the branch's published cap. Anything above the cap is still kept on the entry but doesn't roll into the annual total.
faq_timezoneShift_q: Will my time entries or plans shift days if I travel between timezones?
faq_timezoneShift_a: No. As of the April 2026 update, every time entry and plan is anchored to its calendar date independent of timezone, so traveling or crossing a daylight-saving boundary will not move entries to a different day. Older entries created before that update are migrated automatically the first time you open the new version. If you ever spot an entry on the wrong day after updating, please send a bug report and we'll take a look.
faq_scheduleViews_q: How do I plan across months or see my whole service year?
faq_scheduleViews_a: The Schedule tab has two views; switch between them with the buttons at the top. Month shows your weeks as one calendar you scroll through without stopping at the end of a month, so you can plan this month and next side by side. The month you're reading stays bright and the others fade back, and the two cards above the calendar show that month's and the next month's goal: time logged, time planned, and what's left to plan. Tap a card to scroll to its month, or tap the bright one for goal coverage, schedule pace, and the Assistant. Each day shows the time you planned, or the time you logged once you log some. Tap a day to see or change it, or touch and hold it to add time or plan it. Year shows the twelve months of the service year (September through August), each day colored like the calendar, with your annual goal on top if you have one. Tap a month, or pinch outward, to zoom into it; pinch inward in Month to zoom back out. A labeled line marks where one service year ends and the next begins; tap it to see that year. Use the arrows or swipe to change years, and tap Today to come back. Both views only show what's already in your records; changing views doesn't share anything.
faq_planDetails_q: What's on a Plan's page, and how do I change a Plan?
faq_planDetails_a: Tap a day on the Schedule tab, then tap one of its Plans, or tap a Plan on Home, to open it. Its page shows the date and start time, how long it is, its Type, how often it repeats, the place, and the note; tap the place to open it in Maps. To change the Plan, tap Edit (the pencil). For a recurring plan, saving asks whether the change is for only this date, this and future dates, or all dates. More (•••) holds Duplicate, Log as Time (for today or earlier), Open in Maps, Copy Address, Copy Note, and Delete. With Buddies, the page also lists who you invited and how each answered, plus anyone who asked to join, with Invite. Tap Invite Buddies to invite someone right away while the Plan is still ahead; they get the date, time, title, location, and note. To take someone off, use Edit. For a Plan you joined through a buddy's invitation, the page shows who organized it and your answer. Switch between Going and Can't Make It anytime until a day after the Plan: Can't Make It takes the Plan off your schedule, and Going puts it back.
faq_editRecurringPlan_q: Can I edit or delete a single occurrence of a recurring plan?
faq_editRecurringPlan_a: Yes. On the Schedule tab, tap the day, then tap the plan to open it. To change only that date, tap Edit (the pencil), make your changes, save, and choose Only this date. Changing the Type, title, or location for one date turns that date into its own one-time plan. To remove only that date, tap More (•••), then Delete → Delete This Plan. Your recurring plan stays intact for every other day.
faq_awayDay_q: How do I mark a day I'm not going out without breaking my recurring plan?
faq_awayDay_a: Tap that day's plan on the Schedule tab to open it, tap More (•••), then Delete → Delete This Plan. Only that day is removed, and the recurring plan keeps going from the next day forward. To go out at a different time that day instead, tap Edit, change it, and choose Only this date when you save.
faq_planFirstMonth_q: Can WitnessWork plan my month for me?
faq_planFirstMonth_a: Yes. During setup, if you log hours and have a monthly goal, you get a quick preview of the Assistant: pick the days you usually go out and it spreads your goal across those days for this month, or next month if fewer than seven days are left. Tap any day to change its plan with the slider, or to plan a day yourself. Tap Add to my schedule to save them as plans on the Schedule tab, where you can change or delete any of them, or tap I'll plan later to continue without plans. The weekdays you didn't pick become off days, so the Assistant won't suggest plans on them; change this anytime in Settings → Preferences → Plans → Availability. After setup, you plan on the Schedule tab by tapping any day, and the Assistant there suggests plans whenever you're short of your goal. Plans are saved with your other records and don't count toward your report; log the time you actually spend. Kingdom Publishers who don't log hours, and anyone without a monthly goal, skip this step but can still add plans from the Schedule tab.
faq_importContacts_q: Can I import contacts from my phone's address book?
faq_importContacts_a: Not at this time. Contacts are entered manually in WitnessWork. This keeps your ministry contacts private and avoids accidentally pulling in personal contacts.
faq_importOtherApps_q: Can I import data from MyTime, Ministry Assistant, or another app?
faq_importOtherApps_a: MyTime backups are supported. Open Settings → MyTime Import, choose the original .mytimedb backup from MyTime, and review the preview before importing. Other apps' backup formats are not automatically supported. If you can export readable text, Notes Import may help bring it in with Scribe AI on supported devices when available. Review its proposed records and warnings before saving. WitnessWork JSON backups belong in Settings → Backup & Restore instead.
faq_backupRestore_q: How do I back up and restore my data?
faq_backupRestore_a: Open Settings → Backup & Restore → Create Backup or Restore From Backup to export or restore a JSON backup on iOS or Android. On a new device, you can also choose From a backup file on the “Pick up where you left off” setup screen; restoring there finishes setup with your restored profile. Backups include service records, plans, contacts, visits, categories, profile, and shared preferences. A restore replaces the included local data; older backups may omit categories or profile, which are kept as they are. Device identity, iCloud or Google Drive sync settings, data protection mode, analytics consent, and onboarding progress stay local to this device. Photo files are not embedded in JSON backups. For iCloud photos on iOS, enable photo sync separately. Save a current backup before restoring and keep it in a private location; it can contain householder details. Use the Help Center’s private support option for recovery help.
faq_shareAddress_q: How do I get directions to a contact?
faq_shareAddress_a: Open the contact and tap their address. You'll be offered Apple Maps, Google Maps, or Waze depending on what's installed. You can also pin a contact's location without an address, which is useful for areas where street numbers don't exist.
faq_manualPin_q: My pin is in the wrong place. Can I move it?
faq_manualPin_a: Yes. Open the contact's address screen and drag the pin to the correct spot. You can also place a pin without an address at all, which is helpful in areas without precise geolocation data.
faq_profilePic_q: Can I add a photo to a contact?
faq_profilePic_a: Yes. Open a contact, tap the avatar, and pick a photo from your library or take a new one. This is especially handy when contacts share names or when a photo helps you spot the right door.
faq_dismissContact_q: How do I hide a contact without deleting them?
faq_dismissContact_a: Open the contact and tap "Dismiss." You'll pick how long to dismiss them for (1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, or 1 year). The contact disappears from your active lists for that period and then comes back automatically when the time is up. If notifications are enabled, you'll also get a reminder when they reappear, so dismissed contacts won't quietly slip through the cracks. You can find or restore dismissed contacts at any time from the link at the bottom of your Contacts list, the ••• menu in Contacts, or Settings → Dismissed Contacts.
faq_contactStalenessFilter_q: How do I see which contacts are due for a visit?
faq_contactStalenessFilter_a: Below the search field in Contacts, tap a chip to show only contacts in that group: Stale, This month, This week, or Never contacted. Each chip shows how many active contacts it holds, and its color matches the contact's pin on the map. Swipe the chips sideways to see them all. Tap the chip again, or tap All, to show everyone. The same chips sit at the top of the map, where they count only contacts with a location and filter the pins; they tuck away while you move the map, so tap the Contacts title to bring them back. To change their order, touch a chip, pause briefly, then drag it along the row; All stays first. The order is a preference, so it's included in backups and syncs with iCloud Sync on iOS. Groups are based on your most recent visit, and "Not at homes" count as visits. To change when a contact moves between groups, or the colors, tap the info button at the end of the chips (on the map, the legend button) and then the pencil. A chip adds a filter you can also see and remove in Sort & Filter, and it applies to the list and the map alike. Dismissed contacts aren't counted. Nothing is shared; the groups are worked out on your device.
faq_reportBug_q: How do I report a bug or request a feature?
faq_reportBug_a: Use the buttons below to report a bug or request a feature. Include the steps to reproduce it, what you expected, your device and operating-system version, and the WitnessWork version shown under Still need help?. Remove private contact details, notes, account IDs, and Buddies Codes or invite links from public reports and screenshots. For backup or other sensitive problems, use the private email link in Still need help? instead. Source code, the Privacy Policy, and Terms of Use are under Settings → About.
faq_translations_q: Which languages does WitnessWork support, and how do I report a wrong translation?
faq_translations_a: WitnessWork is available in 18 languages. It follows your device's language by default; to pick another, open Settings and change Language. If your language isn't supported, the app shows English. Translations are made with AI, so a word or phrase may sometimes be off, especially terms Jehovah's Witnesses use in a particular way. To report one, use the email link in Still need help? and include your language, the screen, the text you see, and what it should say. A screenshot helps; cover names, addresses, and notes first. Corrections arrive in a later app update. There is no longer a volunteer translation project to join.
faq_becomeSupporter_q: What do I get as a supporter?
faq_becomeSupporter_a: An active Supporter subscription gives you the Supporter badge, custom accent colors, saved contact views, and Plan Today's Route, which puts the day's follow-ups and plans in the shortest driving order, plus iCloud Sync and alternate app icons on iOS and Google Drive Sync on Android. Supporters also get a larger Scribe AI allowance for Notes Import on iOS and Android where it is available; the current free and Supporter allowances appear in Help and on the support screen. Core features remain free, including contact filters and sorting, and Buddies when available; Supporters can also choose each buddy's color. A one-time Tip gives Donor recognition but does not activate Supporter features.
faq_stillFree_a: Yes — and always will be. Every core feature stays free for everyone. Supporting is completely optional; it helps fund ongoing development and unlocks a few personal touches as a thank-you.
faq_stopSupporting_q: What happens if I stop supporting?
faq_stopSupporting_a: To stop, open Settings → Manage subscription and choose Cancel or change subscription, or cancel in your App Store or Google Play subscriptions. Supporter access continues until the end of the period you've paid for, and your existing data and local backups remain available. After that, iCloud sync pauses while Supporter access is unavailable. If sync was on, it resumes when access returns; an explicit choice to turn it off stays off. Photo sync follows its own setting. Your accent color and app icon return to the defaults, but your choices are kept for when you support again. Saved contact views are hidden and no longer applied, so Contacts shows your own filters; they come back when you support again. Check Settings → iCloud Sync for the current status. If you only need a break, you can pause instead.
faq_pauseSupport_q: Can I pause my support instead of cancelling?
faq_pauseSupport_a: Yes. Open Settings → Manage subscription. On iPhone and iPad, choose to pause payments for 1, 3, or 6 months. The pause starts when your current period ends. You aren't charged during it, and Supporter features stay on, including iCloud Sync, your accent color, and app icon. Payments then resume automatically at the same amount on the date shown, and you can still cancel anytime in your App Store subscriptions. You can pause once every 12 months; the pause dates are saved with your settings so your other devices respect them. On Android, choose Pause in Google Play to pause a monthly subscription for 1 to 3 months. Supporter features such as the badge and accent color pause too, then return automatically with your settings kept, and you can resume early in Google Play. Pause options don't appear during a free trial, a payment problem, a Family Sharing subscription, or within 12 months of your last pause. If a pause fails, nothing changes; try again later or manage your subscription in your store. For anything else, use Still need help? to contact support privately.
faq_acceptDonations_a: As a brother in the hall, I consider it a privilege to be able to use my skills to help others in the congregation. Although free to everyone, developing, running, and maintaining this application, unfortunately costs a significant amount of money and time. I view donating as similar to how one might pay for another's gas after going in service with them - it's a loving gesture that goes greatly appreciated.
faq_donationsUsedFor_q: What are the donations used for?
faq_donationsUsedFor_a: Your donation helps keeps this app running! There are costs with purchasing real devices as development equipment, paying for location API service fees, build service API fees, app store fees, and opportunity cost of my many hours spent developing this app. Each piece of support is greatly appreciated!
faq_whatsNew_q: Where can I see what changed in the latest update?
faq_findNavigation_q: Where are Map, Buddies, and Settings?
faq_findNavigation_a: The bottom bar shows Home, Schedule, Contacts, and Progress, with Add beside them for logging time, creating a Plan, or adding a contact. Progress and Add Time appear when your role logs hours. Map is inside Contacts: tap the map button beside the Contacts title, and WitnessWork opens the view you used last. Buddies, when available on iOS, opens from the Buddies button at the top of Schedule. View Report at the top of Progress opens the Service Report for the month you're viewing. Tap your profile picture at the top left of any main screen for Profile (your role, time served, and stats), Settings, Support, and Help Center; on a wide tablet layout, Settings also stays in the sidebar. If you hid the sidebar, tap Show sidebar in the page header to bring it back. If you turned on Hide Donate Heart, Support is left out of that menu and stays in Settings. Your contacts, plans, and records are unchanged; only where you find them moved. If something still seems missing, update the app, then use Still need help? below.
faq_tabletSidebar_q: How do I resize or hide the sidebar on my tablet?
faq_tabletSidebar_a: On a wide tablet window on iOS or Android, drag the small bar halfway down the sidebar's right edge to resize it. Narrowing the sidebar hides destination names and leaves their icons; widen it to show the names again. Tap Hide sidebar beside WitnessWork (at the top of the icon-only sidebar) to hide navigation completely. Tap Show sidebar in the page header to restore your last saved width. Your width and visibility are saved on this device across app restarts; they are not synced or included in ministry backups, and resizing does not change your records. The sidebar needs a window at least 1,000 points wide and a supported text size. In a narrower window or with very large text, the bottom bar returns automatically; widen the window or rotate to landscape to use the sidebar again. Screen reader users can adjust the Resize sidebar control to increase or decrease its width. If the navigation still seems missing, restart the app and use Still need help? below; keep contact details and other private data out of public reports.
faq_whatsNew_a: Tap your profile picture, then Settings → What's New, for a summary of recent changes. Big updates also open a short tour the first time you launch after updating. If you choose Later, the notification bell keeps a shortcut to it, and What's New has a button to take the tour again.
faq_notificationsTray_q: What's in the bell on Home?
faq_notificationsTray_a: The bell at the top of Home collects reminders and updates, so they wait there instead of piling up on Home when you open the app. You'll find things like last month's Service Report, a pending time rollover, backup and data protection reminders, missed Follow-ups, reminders that already went off, Buddies activity (where Buddies is available), ready Notes Imports, and What's New. The red badge counts items you haven't seen yet. Tap an item to act on it, tap X to dismiss it, or tap Clear All. Invitations and requests still waiting for your answer stay until you respond. A dismissed item doesn't come back. Which items you've seen or dismissed is remembered on this device only.
faq_shareApp_q: How do I share WitnessWork with a friend?
faq_shareApp_a: Tap your profile picture, then Settings → Share WitnessWork. Pick Android or iPhone, and your friend can scan the code with their phone's camera to open WitnessWork in Google Play or the App Store. Share Link sends a message with both store links, so it works for anyone. WitnessWork is free on both. The message only contains the store links — nothing about you or your records. If a code won't scan, turn up your screen's brightness or use Share Link instead.
faq_android_a: Yes. WitnessWork is back on Google Play, and it's free. Time and reports, the timer, contacts and follow-ups, plans, the map (with Google Maps), mileage, reminders, and backups all work on Android. Buddies works on Android too, including with buddies on iPhone. Supporters can keep their Android devices in sync with Google Drive Sync. A few features rely on Apple services and stay on iPhone and iPad: iCloud Sync, widgets, Live Activities, and app icons. Notes Import with Scribe AI is rolling out on Android. To move to a new phone on either platform, create a backup (Settings → Backup & Restore → Create Backup), copy the file to the new phone, then choose From a backup file on the “Pick up where you left off” setup screen. Between Android devices you can also choose From Google Drive there. Keep backup files private; they can contain householder details.
openSourceLicenses_description: WitnessWork is built with {{packages}} open-source packages. Thank you to the people who maintain them. Tap a package to see its license and source.
faq_about_q: Where are the Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, and open-source licenses?
faq_about_a: Tap your profile picture, then Settings, and scroll to About. It links to the Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, and WitnessWork's source code. On devices where Notes Import is available, it also links to the OpenRouter ZDR policy that covers notes you send to Scribe AI. Open Source Licenses lists every open-source package WitnessWork is built with, along with its version, license, and author; tap a package to open its page, which shows the full license and source. Search by package name, license, or author. Long-press any link to copy or share it.
faq_debugTools_a: Debugging Tools helps troubleshoot problems with support. Turn it on in Settings → Advanced; it applies only to the device you turn it on for, on iOS and Android. It adds a Tools tab with diagnostic, test-data, and repair actions, shows extra technical details on some screens, and turns on more detailed diagnostic logging. Some Tools actions add sample data or permanently delete data, so only use them when support asks, and back up first under Settings → Backup & Restore. Turning the switch on or off doesn't change your data; turn it off to hide the Tools tab and details again.
faq_backupRecovery_q: My backup looks unreadable or my restored records are missing. What should I do?
faq_backupRecovery_a: A WitnessWork backup is structured JSON for the app to read, so it does not look like a printable Service Report. Keep the original file unchanged and restore it through Settings → Backup & Restore → Restore From Backup. If records are missing, preserve the original backup and create a separate backup of the device's current data before trying another restore. Email support with the app version and what happened; arrange any file sharing privately. Backup files can contain contact details and notes, so keep them out of public bug reports.
faq_syncTroubleshooting_q: My devices are not syncing. What can I check?
faq_syncTroubleshooting_a: On iOS, use the same Apple Account, turn on iCloud Drive, and enable WitnessWork under iCloud on each device. On Android, see “Google Drive Sync isn’t working on my Android device. What can I check?” iCloud sync requires Supporter access. Open Settings → iCloud Sync and use Sync now. Changes waiting to be sent are retried; an unreadable file or newer app version is shown in the status, so update every device and try again. The status shows Uploading to iCloud until Apple confirms the upload, and Last synced counts only confirmed uploads. If your iCloud storage is full, changes stay on this device; free up space or upgrade your storage in Settings → [Your Name] → iCloud and uploading resumes on its own. Keep an exported backup and the device containing your latest data. Rebuild iCloud data replaces the iCloud data with this device’s data and removes iCloud photos it doesn’t use. Your other devices switch to that data the next time they sync, replacing changes made on them before then, and the Home bell notes it. Update WitnessWork on every device first: an older version keeps its own data until it is updated. Contact private support from the Help Center if syncing remains incomplete. Keep householder details out of public reports.
faq_syncPhotos_q: Why are contact photos missing on my other device?
faq_syncPhotos_a: Photo sync is an optional Supporter feature on iOS and Android. Open Settings → iCloud Sync (Google Drive Sync on Android) and turn on Include images in sync. This uploads profile and contact photos to your private iCloud container (or WitnessWork's hidden Google Drive folder) and downloads referenced photos; they count against your iCloud or Google storage. Update WitnessWork on every device to use photo revisions safely. Pausing photo sync on one device keeps the uploaded files and local copies. To remove uploaded photos, choose Remove iCloud photos and pause photo sync on other devices first, or they can upload their copies again. Removing a contact or its photo removes downloaded copies when that change arrives; obsolete cloud copies are cleaned up after a one-day grace period. If a photo is missing, keep the device with the original, check storage and permissions, then use Sync now. Use the Help Center’s private support option if it still fails; do not include householder information in public reports.
faq_mytimeTrouble_q: MyTime Import says the file is not a database. What should I use?
faq_mytimeTrouble_a: MyTime Import needs an original .mytimedb backup created by MyTime. A PDF, text export, WitnessWork JSON backup, or a file renamed to .mytimedb will not work. Save a complete copy of the MyTime backup on your device and select it through Settings → MyTime Import. Keep the original file unchanged. If a valid backup still fails, email support privately with the error and app version; do not post the backup in a public issue.
faq_notesImportHelp_q: How does Notes Import work, and what does it cost?
faq_notesImportHelp_a: When Notes Import is available on your supported iPhone, iPad, or Android device, open it from Settings and paste readable ministry notes. On iPhone and iPad you can also record a voice log or scan a photo of your notes. Scribe AI proposes contacts, visits, and time entries; review the preview, assumptions, and warnings before saving selected records. The Help button explains what to include and shows the current free and Supporter allowances. Failed, cancelled, and repeated imports do not count toward the allowance. Voice logs and photos are turned into text on your device first. Your notes are sent to a language-model service under a Zero Data Retention arrangement; import history stays on this device. Find the OpenRouter ZDR policy in the Notes Import Help or under Settings → About. On Android it is rolling out gradually and needs WitnessWork from Google Play; see Does Notes Import work on Android?
faq_notesImportRetry_q: Notes Import failed, is still working, or found no records. What should I do?
faq_notesImportRetry_a: Check your internet connection and follow any Update WitnessWork message. If an import is still working, reopen Notes Import and check its history before starting another copy. For too much text, use smaller batches; if Scribe AI cannot interpret it, add clear names, dates, and time spent, then retry. If the service is temporarily unavailable, try later. A preview with no records means nothing was found to import. Review the preview before saving, and email support privately if the error continues.
faq_notesImportAndroid_q: Does Notes Import work on Android?
faq_notesImportAndroid_a: Yes, as it rolls out. When Notes Import appears in Settings on your Android phone or tablet, it works as it does on iPhone: paste readable notes, review what Scribe AI proposes, and save the records you choose. Voice logs and photo import aren't available on Android, so type or paste your notes. It needs WitnessWork installed from Google Play on a Play Protect certified device, with the Google Play Store and Google Play services up to date. Before each import, Google Play Integrity checks that the app and device are genuine. Google receives that check from your device and an unreadable fingerprint of the import, never your notes; your notes go only to the Scribe AI service described in How does Notes Import work. Rooted devices, custom system software, emulators, and modified or unofficial copies of the app can't be verified. If Scribe AI asks you to update Google Play, update the Google Play Store and Google Play services, then try again. If it can't verify your device, reinstall WitnessWork from Google Play and try again; if it still can't, Notes Import isn't supported on that device. Free and Supporter allowances are the same as on iPhone. Supporter status comes from the store you subscribed in, so an App Store subscription doesn't unlock it on Android. If Notes Import doesn't appear, update WitnessWork; it may not have reached your device yet. For anything else, use the Help Center's private support link and keep your notes out of public reports.
faq_notesImportVoicePhoto_q: How do voice logs and photo imports work, and what leaves my device?
faq_notesImportVoicePhoto_a: In Notes Import, tap the microphone to record a voice log. For example, after a call, say who you talked with, what you discussed, and when you plan to go back, then tap the check mark. Or tap the camera to scan handwritten notes or a house-to-house record, or to choose up to five photos. Speech and handwriting are turned into text on your device, and the text appears in the message box so you can fix anything misheard or misread before you send it. Audio and photos are never saved or uploaded. Only the text you send goes to Scribe AI, just like pasted notes, and each new import uses an Import Credit. A voice log stops after 10 minutes, and the microphone appears only when this device supports on-device speech recognition for your app or device language. The first recording in a language may wait while your device downloads Apple's speech model. Recording needs microphone access, plus speech recognition access before iOS 26. Scanning needs camera access; choosing photos needs no extra permission. If you denied access, turn on Microphone, Speech Recognition, or Camera for WitnessWork in your device's Settings. If nothing is recognized, try again somewhere quieter or with a flat, well-lit page, or type or paste your notes instead. If it keeps failing, email support privately from Still need help? in the Help Center. Voice logs and photo import work only on iPhone and iPad; on Android, type or paste your notes instead.
faq_hourglassSetup_q: How do I send my report to Hourglass or NW Publisher?
faq_hourglassSetup_a: Open the month's Service Report, choose Hourglass or NW Publisher in the dropdown above Submit, and tap Submit. Review and send the report in the destination app. Copy and Share are also available. NW Publisher accepts only the previous month's report. Hourglass receives preaching time separately, with Credit Time included in the default report comment; if you replace the comment, check that it still says what you need. Update WitnessWork if a submission option is missing.
faq_savedContactViews_q: Can I save a contact filter and switch to it quickly?
faq_savedContactViews_a: Yes, with saved views, a Supporter feature on iOS and Android. In Contacts, tap the filter button beside search (or ••• → Sort & Filter…), choose filters and a sort, then tap Save as view at the top and name it (up to 30 characters), such as Bible studies or Spanish territory.
