Your views appear as buttons under the search field, above the last-visit chips, and at the top of the map: tap one to show it, and tap it again to return to your own filters. A view applies to the list and the map alike. Search text isn't saved in a view. While a view is showing, changes you make in Sort & Filter or with the last-visit chips are marked Edited; tap Update view to keep them, Save as new view to keep both, or Reset to discard them. To reorder your views, touch one, pause briefly, then drag it along the row. Touch and hold a view without moving to rename or delete it, or choose ••• → Edit Saved Views to rename, reorder, and delete views. Deleting a view never changes your contacts. Renaming or archiving a contact field keeps views working; if you permanently delete a field, filters on it are ignored. Views are stored on your device, included in backups, and sync with iCloud Sync on iOS and Google Drive Sync on Android; update WitnessWork on each device to see them there. Which view is showing stays on each device. Building filters without saving them stays free. If Supporter access ends, your views are hidden from Contacts and no longer applied, but they're kept and come back when access returns. If a view shows unexpected contacts, open Sort & Filter to check its filters, or tap Reset to undo unsaved changes. For anything else, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.
faq_conversationFields_q: Can I track extra details on a conversation, like the publication I used?
faq_conversationFields_a: Yes. Open Preferences → Conversation Fields, or tap Add Custom Fields on the conversation form, and add a field such as Publication. Field names can be up to 14 characters. Every field appears on the form for conversations and Not at Home visits; leave it empty when it doesn't apply. Saved values show on that visit in the contact's history. You can rename and reorder fields any time without losing what you entered. Archiving a field hides it but keeps its values. Delete it from the Archived list to remove the field and its values from every conversation for good. Fields and values stay on your device, are included in backups, and sync between devices with iCloud Sync on iOS; update WitnessWork on each device to see them there. They aren't included when you share a contact. Contact fields are managed separately in Preferences → Contact Fields. With data protection mode on, don't record religion, health, family situation, language, or ethnicity. If a field is missing from the form, check whether it was archived. For anything else, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.
faq_followUpReminders_q: Can I keep visit notes without scheduling a return visit or reminder?
faq_followUpReminders_a: Yes. When adding or editing a visit, turn off Follow Up and save. The visit and its notes remain, but that visit has no scheduled follow-up or reminder and will not appear as overdue. You can turn Follow Up on later and choose a date and time. To stop an older follow-up reminder, edit that visit and turn Follow Up off.
faq_followUpCard_q: How do I use the Today's Conversations card on Home?
faq_followUpCard_a: The card shows the follow-ups you scheduled for today. From 5 PM it shows Upcoming Conversations, which adds tomorrow's; those can be rescheduled but not logged until their day. Swipe sideways to move between people. When you've been, tap Talked to log the conversation in the visit form, or tap Not at Home to log the attempt right away. Undo appears below the card for a few seconds after Not at Home. The calendar button reschedules the follow-up. Use the ••• button or touch and hold a person for call, message, directions, and Dismiss Follow-Up. A follow-up counts as done once you log any visit with that person on or after its day. The bar at the top fills as you go, and the card shows All caught up when every one is done. Tap Done, or touch and hold the title and choose Close for Now, to hide the card until you add or reschedule a follow-up. A follow-up still open 4 hours after its time moves to missed follow-ups in the notifications tray. Not at Home is unavailable while data protection mode is on. Visits are saved like any other visit on this device. To remove the card for good, touch and hold its title and choose Hide This Section, or turn it back on in Customize Home. If something looks wrong, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.
faq_reminders_q: How do follow-up, plan, and contact reminders work?
faq_reminders_a: Turn on Notify Me when adding or editing a Follow-up or a one-time Plan, then choose how long before it starts the reminder should arrive. Dismissing a contact also reminds you when they're available again. If Notify Me is off because notifications aren't allowed, turning it on asks for permission; if you've declined before, it opens your device settings. If the reminder time has already passed, the form says so and no reminder is sent. Rescheduling keeps the reminder time you chose. When a reminder arrives, it is also listed in the Home bell, even if system notifications are off, and tapping either one opens the follow-up, plan, or contact. Each device schedules its own reminders from your saved records, so after iCloud sync or a backup restore, open WitnessWork once on that device to set them up. Deleting a visit, plan, or contact removes its reminders, including any already shown. With data protection mode on, reminders leave out names and topics. On Android, the system may deliver a reminder a few minutes late to save battery. If reminders don't arrive, check that notifications are allowed for WitnessWork in Preferences and in your device settings, and that Focus or Do Not Disturb isn't silencing them. If they still don't arrive, report the problem from the Help Center without including names or other private details.
faq_appIconBadge_q: Why is there a number on the WitnessWork app icon?
faq_appIconBadge_a: On iOS, the number on the app icon is how many items in the Home notification bell you haven't read yet. Open the bell and scroll through it to mark items read; dismissing or clearing them also lowers the number. It updates while WitnessWork is open and when a Follow-up, Plan, or contact reminder arrives. Other items, like last month's report or Buddies activity, are counted the next time you open WitnessWork, so the number can be behind while the app is closed. Each device keeps its own count. The number needs notification permission; to hide it, turn off Badges for WitnessWork in your device's notification settings. On Android, the app icon doesn't show an unread count; your launcher may show a dot for notifications in the notification shade. If the number looks wrong, open WitnessWork, then leave it to refresh the count. If it still doesn't match the bell, contact support from the Help Center.
faq_soundEffects_q: How do I turn off celebration and reminder sounds?
faq_soundEffects_a: Open Settings → Preferences → Audio & Haptics and turn off Play sounds. This controls celebration chimes and reminders while WitnessWork is open; reminders still appear, just without sound (on Android, as a short message in the app). Reminders received while the app is closed follow your device's notification settings; adjust those separately if needed.
faq_haptics_q: How do I turn off vibrations?
faq_haptics_a: Open Settings → Preferences → Audio & Haptics and turn off Haptics. WitnessWork then stops all of its vibration feedback, such as taps, chart scrubbing, and goal celebrations. The setting applies only to this device and isn't synced to your other devices. Some system controls, like menus and switches, may still vibrate based on your device's own settings; adjust those in your device's sound and haptics settings.
faq_routePlanning_q: How do I plan the shortest route for today's stops?
faq_routePlanning_a: Route planning is a Supporter feature on iPhone, iPad, and Android, and it needs an internet connection. On Home, tap Plan Route at the top of the conversations card. You can also tap today's date on Home or in Schedule (on iPad, today's details show beside the calendar), then tap Plan Today's Route. It appears when at least two of today's stops have a map location. Anyone can open it to see today's stops; finding the shortest order needs Supporter. Stops are today's open follow-ups and today's plans. Follow-ups already answered by a visit today, and follow-ups for dismissed contacts, aren't included. A stop without an address or pin isn't included either; add an address or place a pin on the contact or plan location to include it. Choose where to start, either your current location or one of the stops, remove any stops you'll skip, and tap Find Shortest Route. A route can have up to 10 stops, and you can plan up to 10 routes in any 24 hours. The order is the fastest drive with current traffic. Follow-up and plan times aren't considered, so check the order against any fixed appointments. If no route is found, remove stops that can't be reached by car. If planning is unavailable, try again later. Planning a route never changes your contacts, follow-ups, or plans. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support option and keep householder details out of public reports.
faq_routePlanningNavigation_q: How does my route open in Apple Maps, Google Maps, or Waze?
faq_routePlanningNavigation_a: Your route opens in the Default Navigation App chosen in Settings → Navigation. Google Maps opens the whole route as one trip with every stop in order. Apple Maps does the same on iOS 18.4 or later; on earlier versions it opens one stop at a time. Waze always opens one stop at a time because its links accept only a single destination. When stops open one at a time, tap Navigate to Stop 1, then come back to WitnessWork and tap the button again for the next stop, or tap the arrow beside any stop. Each trip starts from where you are, so a stop you chose as the start is simply the first stop. If Google Maps isn't installed, the route opens in a web browser, which may show fewer stops; install the app or choose another navigation app. On Android, choose Google Maps or Waze. If a map app doesn't open, check that it's installed and try again.
faq_routePlanningPrivacy_q: What's shared when I plan a route?
faq_routePlanningPrivacy_a: To find the order, WitnessWork sends the map coordinates of your starting point and each stop to the WitnessWork server, which passes only those coordinates to HERE, a mapping service, to calculate the drive. Names, addresses, notes, topics, and visit details are never sent. The request also carries the app's random account identifier, the one tied to your Supporter purchase, so the server can confirm Supporter status and count your routes; it isn't sent to HERE. The server doesn't store coordinates. It keeps only the times of your route requests from the last 24 hours to apply the daily limit. When you open the route, your navigation app receives each stop's address, or its coordinates for a pin you placed, just as it does when you navigate to a single contact. Usage analytics record counts such as how many stops a route had, never locations.
faq_locationTrouble_q: Why can't the map find my current location?
faq_locationTrouble_a: Check that location services are on and WitnessWork has location permission in your device's settings. Reopen the map and try again where your device can obtain a location. You can still enter an address or place a contact's pin manually without using your current location. If the problem continues, report the error with your device and operating-system version, leaving private contact details out of screenshots.
faq_mapFilters_q: Why are some contacts missing from the map?
faq_mapFilters_a: The map shows your active contacts that have an address or a pin, and it uses the same filters as your Contacts list. Last-visit chips, Saved Views, and filters from Sort & Filter all apply to both, so a contact hidden from the list is hidden from the map too. The chips at the top of the map show what's on; tap All, tap the selected Saved View again, or open ••• → Sort & Filter… and tap Reset to see everyone. If the chips are tucked away after you move the map, tap the Contacts title to bring them back. The map's own search only narrows the pins further and doesn't change the list. A contact you create by dropping a pin stays on the map until you switch to the list, even if your filters would hide it. Dismissed contacts don't appear; find them under ••• → Dismissed Contacts. A contact without an address or pin can't appear either; open the contact and add an address or place its pin. This works the same on iOS and Android, and filters are worked out on your device; nothing is shared. If a contact is still missing, check its address, then contact support from the Help Center and leave out names and addresses.
faq_restoreSupporter_q: I already paid, but Supporter features or prices are missing. What should I do?
faq_restoreSupporter_a: Check your connection and that your device's store uses the account you purchased with. Open Settings → Become a supporter and use Restore Purchases when it is shown. A one-time Tip does not activate Supporter features. If no purchases are found, prices do not load, or your subscription still is not recognized, email support privately with your app version and what happened. If support needs your account ID, use the support button in this screen's header to open Still need help?, then tap Copy Account ID. Share that ID privately. Restoring purchases restores access, not your service records.
faq_foundingSupporter_a: Founding Supporters were already supporting WitnessWork before the Supporter tier launched in May 2026, when support came with no perks at all. The label is simply our thank-you. It isn't a separate tier: Founding Supporters get the same features as every other Supporter, and it can't be purchased or earned now. While your support is active, Founding Supporter appears on your profile and in Settings. It comes from your Supporter start date, so nothing extra is stored or shared. If your support lapses, the label is hidden until you support again. It returns if your store account still reports your original start date, which is usually the case when you resubscribe with the same account. If you expected to see it, open Settings → Become a supporter and use Restore Purchases. If it still doesn't appear, use the support button in this screen's header to open Still need help? and contact support privately.
faq_buddiesOverview_q: What is WitnessWork Buddies, and why don't I see it?
faq_buddiesOverview_a: Buddies lets you connect with up to five people you go out in service with and see each other's planned days, start times, and durations for the next eight weeks. It works on iPhone, iPad, and Android, and buddies on different platforms can connect with each other. On the Schedule calendar, a buddy's photo or initial on a day means you're going out together, and a small dot under a day means other buddies plan to go out. Tap the day to see who. On iPhone and iPad, the Calendar widget shows the same marks and updates when WitnessWork refreshes Buddies, so open the app if it looks behind. It is free when available. Open Schedule, tap Buddies at the top, and complete the introduction with your profile name. A dot on that button means a request is waiting for you to confirm. Buddies may be unavailable during rollout. Update the installed app if the Buddies button is missing. If the button is dimmed, Buddies is temporarily unavailable; your saved buddies stay on your calendar, so try again later.
faq_buddiesAdd_q: How do I add a buddy, and who confirms the request?
faq_buddiesAdd_a: Open Buddies and tap Invite a Buddy or the + button to share a Buddies Invite. To pair in person, use the code button to show your Buddies Code and have the other person scan it inside WitnessWork. You can also paste a link through Enter Invite Link. The recipient taps Accept; the person who created the invite then opens Buddies → Requests and taps Confirm. You start seeing each other's plans only after that confirmation. Confirm only the person you intended to invite.
faq_buddiesInviteTrouble_q: Why is my Buddies Invite waiting, expired, or saying all spots are in use?
faq_buddiesInviteTrouble_a: An accepted request waits until the inviter confirms it in Buddies → Requests. Each Buddies Invite works once and expires after seven days; ask for a new link if it was used, cancelled, or expired. Your five spots include buddies and pending invites or requests. Cancel an unused invite or remove a buddy to make room. Only a limited number of unused invite links can be open at once. If tapping an invite link opens a web page instead of WitnessWork, install WitnessWork from the App Store or Google Play and tap the link again, or copy the link and paste it in Buddies → Enter Invite Link. If scanning is unavailable, allow camera access in your device's settings or share and paste the invite link instead.
faq_buddiesPrivacy_q: What can my buddies see, and is sharing private?
faq_buddiesPrivacy_a: Automatic calendar sharing includes your name and planned days, start times, and durations for the next eight weeks. Photo, pioneer status, and your streak are optional; change them in Buddies Settings. This calendar sharing does not include your recorded service time, reports, goals, categories, contact list, visit history, or notes. Shared content is end-to-end encrypted so only you and the buddies you choose can read it. Explicit Plan and Follow-up invitations share extra details, including a Plan's note or a Follow-up's address; check those details before inviting someone. Find the Privacy Policy under Still need help?, using the support button in this screen's header.
faq_buddiesAskToJoin_q: How do I ask to join a buddy's Plan?
faq_buddiesAskToJoin_a: Tap a day on your Schedule calendar, then tap Ask to Join next to a buddy who plans to go out that day. You can also tap one of their days under Next two weeks on their details screen. Your request shares only what you already see: the day, time, and length of their Plan. It shows as Asked until your buddy invites you, you withdraw it, or the Plan starts; tap Asked to withdraw it. Asking closes two hours before the Plan starts, and you can have up to three requests waiting with each buddy. Your buddy is alerted only the first time you ask for a Plan, and for at most three requests a day. If they move or remove that Plan, your request is withdrawn for you. Asked shows only on the device you asked from. When your buddy invites you, answer in the notification bell on Home. If you choose Going while you already have your own Plan at that time, you can replace it so your time isn't counted twice.
faq_buddiesJoinRequests_q: How do I answer or turn off requests to join my Plans?
faq_buddiesJoinRequests_a: When a buddy asks to join one of your Plans, their request appears in the notification bell on Home. Tap Invite to add them to your Plan and send the invitation right away; the button turns into a check. Tap the request itself to open the Plan, where Invite works the same way. Tap Not Now (or dismiss it) to clear it quietly: your buddy is never told, and the request lapses when the Plan starts. If the Plan came from someone else's invitation, only its organizer can invite. If your Plans that day changed since they asked, open the Plan you're keeping to invite them. To stop alerts for every request, turn off Ask to Join Alerts in Buddies Settings. To stop alerts from one buddy, turn off Ask to Join Alerts on their details screen, or long-press their request and choose Turn Off Alerts. Requests still appear in the bell either way. Not Now and these settings apply to this device only, so a request you cleared on one device can still show on another.
faq_buddiesInvitations_q: How do I invite a buddy to a Plan or Follow-up, and answer an invitation?
faq_buddiesInvitations_a: Use Invite Buddies when adding or editing a Plan or scheduled Follow-up, select confirmed buddies, and save. On a Plan's page, Invite Buddies invites someone right away. You can also tap Invite to a Plan on a buddy's page. A Plan invite shares its date, time, duration, title, location, and note. A Follow-up invite shares its date/time, the householder's first name, address or pin, and topic; those details expire a day after the visit. Check that you want to share these details with the people selected. Follow-up invitations are unavailable in Data Protection Mode. To reply, choose Going or Can't Make It in the notification bell on Home, on the buddy's page in Buddies, or on the Plan's page (tap the invitation in the bell to open it); you can change your answer later. An invitation stays in the bell until you answer it or it is canceled or expires, so it can't be dismissed or cleared by mistake; once answered, you can dismiss it. Going to a Plan adds a linked Plan to your schedule, which follows the inviter's changes or cancellation. Can't Make It takes it off your schedule, and switching back to Going on the Plan's page puts it back. A Follow-up invite does not import the contact or visit history.
faq_buddiesDetail_q: What's on a buddy's page, and can I rename them or change their color?
faq_buddiesDetail_a: Open Buddies and tap a buddy. Needs your answer lists their invitations you haven't answered; choose Going or Can't Make It there or in the Home notification bell. Together lists upcoming Plans and Follow-ups between you two, whoever invited whom, with each answer; tap a Plan to open its page, or use the menu on a buddy's invitation to change your answer. Next two weeks shows the days your buddy plans to go out next to your own; tap one of their days to plan the same time or ask to join. Invite to a Plan opens a new Plan with that buddy already invited, and View on Calendar opens Schedule. A nickname is a private name only you see; your buddy isn't told, and clearing it brings back their own name. Supporters can choose a buddy's color from the same swatches as the accent color, or any color with the eyedropper; Default brings back the color given when you paired, which everyone else keeps. Nicknames and colors are kept with your encrypted Buddies data, so they return when Buddies restores on another device. Their full schedule for the next eight weeks is on your calendar while Show on my calendar is on.
faq_buddiesMissingPlans_q: Why are a buddy's plans or invitations missing or out of date?
faq_buddiesMissingPlans_a: Check that the request has been confirmed and Show on my calendar is on for that buddy. Calendar sharing covers only the next eight weeks. Both people need an internet connection to send and receive changes; open Buddies and pull down to refresh. Previously downloaded plans remain viewable offline, but new changes need a connection; Buddies says when you're offline or it couldn't refresh. Seeing a buddy's calendar does not add their plans to yours. Turn on Buddies notifications in Buddies Settings and your device's notification settings, and check the Home notification bell for invitations even if no notification arrived. On Android, Buddies notifications need Google Play services; without them, changes still arrive when you open WitnessWork. The bell checks for new Buddies activity when you open it and when you return to WitnessWork; if it says it couldn't check, reconnect and tap Try Again.
faq_buddiesNotSent_q: Why does my answer say Sending in or Not sent yet, or my request say Waiting to Send?
faq_buddiesNotSent_a: Going is sent to your buddy right away. Can't Make It waits 15 seconds first, in case you tapped it by mistake: tap Change to fix it before it's sent. Leaving the app sends it right away. Not sent yet or Waiting to Send means your answer or Ask to Join request hasn't reached your buddy, usually because you're offline or Buddies is temporarily unavailable. You don't need to answer or ask again: it's saved on this device and sends automatically the next time Buddies refreshes, such as when you open Buddies or return to WitnessWork while connected. To send it sooner, reconnect, open Buddies, and pull down to refresh. Your buddy won't see the answer or request until it's sent.
faq_buddiesRemove_q: How do I hide a buddy, stop sharing, or delete my Buddies data?
faq_buddiesRemove_a: Open a buddy's details and turn off Show on my calendar to hide their plans on this device; sharing continues, and your own Plans with them still show. Remove Buddy ends the connection for both people, and reconnecting takes a new invite. They are not notified, though they may notice. If removal is pending while offline, they may still see your last shared plans until WitnessWork reconnects and completes it. Buddies Settings → Delete My Buddies Data removes all connections and invites and erases your encrypted Buddies data and encryption identity. It cannot be undone; reconnect and retry if deletion is pending. Your personal service records and contacts remain.
faq_buddiesRestore_q: Can I recover my buddies on another device or from a backup?
faq_buddiesRestore_a: On iPhone and iPad, your Buddies encryption key is kept in iCloud Keychain, so Buddies restores its connections on another device using the same Apple Account, or after you reinstall WitnessWork, when it syncs. On Android, Google Play services keeps the key: it comes back when you reinstall WitnessWork on the same phone while Google backup is on (Settings → Google → Backup), and with a screen lock set it's also saved, end-to-end encrypted, in your Google backup, so it can return when you set up a new phone from that backup. Without a screen lock, the key stays on that phone. Android devices don't share one key the way iCloud Keychain does, so each Android device, and an iPhone and an Android phone, have their own Buddies connections. Regular WitnessWork backup files do not contain the encryption key. Buddies recovery is separate from Supporter iCloud Sync for service records. If the key is unavailable, or you used Delete My Buddies Data, reconnect with new invites. Keep your personal records backed up separately.
faq_mileageStart_a: Mileage Tracking is optional and available for every publisher type. Answer Yes on the "Track mileage?" card on Home, or turn on Track Mileage in Settings → Preferences → Publisher. Then add your first car; only a name is required. Log a trip with Log Trip on Home's Mileage card, from the Add button, or on the Mileage screen. Enter the distance (turn on Round Trip to double it) or switch to Odometer and enter start and end readings. Odometer Start fills in from that car's last reading. Trips can't be dated in the future. Tap a trip to see its details, or long-press it to edit, log it again today, share, or delete it.
faq_mileageCost_q: How is the estimated fuel cost calculated, and what happens when fuel prices change?
faq_mileageCost_a: Estimated fuel cost is distance ÷ the car's fuel economy × its fuel's price, using the values in effect on each trip's date. It only appears once the car has a fuel economy and its fuel has a price; trips without both are left out and the report says so. A fuel's price is shared by every car that uses that fuel. When you change a price or a car's fuel economy, choose From a Date to apply it from that day forward (earlier trips keep the old value) or Fix Current Value to correct a mistake, which also updates the past trips that used it. Each fuel and car keeps a history; long-press an entry to delete it. The amount is only an estimate. If you're reimbursed, the actual amount is calculated by whoever reimburses you.
faq_mileageUnits_q: Can I use kilometers, litres, or L/100 km?
faq_mileageUnits_a: Yes. Open Mileage → Settings (the gear) → Units. Distance can be miles or kilometers, and fuel economy can be mpg (US), mpg (UK), L/100 km, or km/L. Auto follows your device's region. Fuel is priced per gallon with mpg (US) and per litre with every other choice. Currency follows your device's region. Changing units only changes how numbers are shown; your trips aren't altered.
faq_mileageShare_q: How do I share or export my mileage report?
faq_mileageShare_a: Open Mileage, choose Day, Week, Month, or Year (service year, September to August), and use the arrows or swipe to pick the period. Tap the share button at the top to Copy the report, Share it as text, or Export CSV for a spreadsheet. The text lists totals, per-car totals when you have more than one car, and each trip except in the Year view. The CSV has one row per trip with the car, odometer readings, distance, note, fuel, fuel economy, price, and estimated cost. Trip notes are included, so check them before sending. To share one trip, open it and tap the share button.
faq_mileageCars_q: What's the difference between archiving and deleting a car?
faq_mileageCars_a: Open Mileage → Settings, tap the car, and choose Archive or Delete…. Archiving hides the car from new trips but keeps its trips in your reports; unarchive it anytime from Archived Cars. Deleting removes the car and all of its trips on every device that syncs with this one, and can't be undone. Deleting a fuel removes its price history, so cars using it stop showing an estimated cost.
faq_mileageSync_q: Does my mileage sync, and does it work on Android?
faq_mileageSync_a: Mileage works on iOS and Android. Cars, fuels, prices, and trips sync between iOS devices with iCloud Sync, which is a Supporter feature, and they're included in backups from Settings → Backup & Restore on both platforms. On Android they sync between Android devices with Google Drive Sync, also a Supporter feature. Between an iPhone and an Android device, use a backup. Mileage is never shared with Buddies and doesn't appear on your calendar or Service Report.
faq_mileageTurnOff_q: How do I turn mileage tracking on or off?
faq_mileageChart_q: What does the chart on the Mileage screen show?
faq_mileageChart_a: Open the Mileage screen and choose Week, Month, or Year. The chart shows how far you drove each day, or each month of the service year (September through August). When more than one car has trips in that period, each bar is split by car, using the colors next to each car's total. Tap a bar to open that day or month and see its trips. The Day view has no chart, and a period without trips shows none. Bars show distance, not estimated cost.
faq_mileageTurnOff_a: Use the Track Mileage switch in Settings → Preferences → Publisher. Turning it off hides the Home card, the Log Trip action, and the Mileage screen, but keeps your trips; turn it back on and everything returns. If you chose No Thanks on the Home card, this switch turns it on anytime. To erase your mileage, open Mileage → Settings → Delete All Mileage Data. This deletes it on every device that syncs with this one and can't be undone. You can also hide only the Home card with Settings → Preferences → Home Screen.

faq_syncRecovery_q: What happens to setup choices, deleted contacts, and reminders during sync?
faq_syncRecovery_a: Restart onboarding affects only this device. Choosing Set up fresh pauses iCloud sync until you explicitly enable it in Settings; then choose Merge both or Restore from iCloud as appropriate. Restore from iCloud reads other devices’ snapshots and replaces local data after confirmation. During onboarding, a device that already has records asks before replacing them, and Supporters can choose Merge instead. Keep this device’s data makes your other devices switch to this device’s data the next time they sync, replacing changes made on them before then. Restoring data does not send Buddies declines for plans absent from the backup. Recoverable deleted contact details are retained for up to 90 days, then removed while deletion evidence remains. Reminders are rebuilt on this device after merges and restores, keeping the reminder time chosen for each follow-up and plan; notification permission is required and only future reminders are scheduled. For recovery, keep the device with the latest records and export a backup before replacing data. Use private Help Center support if you need help.
faq_syncRemoveDevice_q: How do I remove an old device from iCloud sync?
faq_syncRemoveDevice_a: Each device that uses iCloud Sync keeps its own copy of your data in your iCloud, and that copy stays after you stop using the device, even after a reinstall or a new phone. Remove it when you no longer use a device, for example one you sold, replaced, or reset. On a device that still syncs, open Settings → iCloud Sync → Devices and tap Remove beside the old device. Devices not synced in 90 or more days are marked. Removing deletes only that device’s copy from iCloud, including details it still held of contacts deleted elsewhere. This device keeps everything it has already synced, and your other devices aren’t changed. If the removed device is still in use, it adds its data back the next time it syncs; turn off iCloud Sync on it first if you want it to stop. Before removing a device, this device must finish syncing its data; if asked, go back, tap Sync now, and fix any problem the status shows. If the device uses a newer version of WitnessWork, update this device first. Devices replaced by Rebuild iCloud data can be removed at any time. Photos aren’t stored per device, so removing a device doesn’t remove photos; use Remove iCloud photos for that. Devices is part of iCloud Sync on iOS and Google Drive Sync on Android (Settings → Google Drive Sync → Devices), both Supporter features; on Android the copies are in your Google Drive. If you need help, use the Help Center’s private support option and keep householder details out of public reports.
